data.reasoning: Both models correctly identified the PKGBUILD as a standard binary package with pinned SHA256 checksums fetching from the official upstream GitHub repository, and .SRCINFO as standard metadata. The disagreement stems solely from a tool error (HTTP 400 API failure) in qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 when reviewing .cspell.json. The package contains no injection patterns, no execution of fetched content, and no suspicious network operations.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error (LLM API HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 when attempting to audit .cspell.json, resulting in an INCONCLUSIVE status for that file. deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed the same file and correctly identified it as a benign spell checker configuration. This is not a genuine security disagreement but rather a tool failure on a non-security-relevant file.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 experienced an API error (HTTP 400) when reviewing .cspell.json, resulting in INCONCLUSIVE status
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) on non-security-relevant files should not result in INCONCLUSIVE overall verdicts; the audit tool should distinguish between security-relevant files (PKGBUILD, .install, patches) and development/editor configs

The audit tool should implement fallback logic: when a tool error occurs on a file that is not referenced by PKGBUILD functions and is clearly a development config (like .cspell.json, .editorconfig, CI configs), it should not block the final verdict
File selection logic should prioritize security-relevant files and deprioritize or skip development tooling configs unless they are explicitly referenced in build/install hooks
